title: Insta360 Luna Gimbal Camera Gives You the Steady Shots Your Audience Deserves
gist: WIRED rates Insta360's Luna Pro ($600) and Luna Ultra ($770) gimbal cameras 7/10 and calls them probably the best gimbal camera buyable in the US, partly because DJI's competing Osmo Pocket 4 line is not officially sold there amid a US lawsuit.

insights.claim: Insta360 and DJI are in a US court fight over the Luna and Osmo Pocket 4 cameras, and DJI's cameras are not officially available in the US, which makes Insta360's Luna series the more compelling buy.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.so_what: Litigation and availability, not just specs, are shaping competitive position in consumer gimbal cameras.
insights.quote: the two companies are currently butting heads in a US court over these and other cameras

insights.claim: The Luna Pro is likely the better value for most users, saving $170 versus the Ultra in exchange for losing the 3X optical zoom lens.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.so_what: Mid-tier SKU captures most demand; zoom is a niche upsell.

insights.claim: Both Luna models use a 1-inch sensor with a 20-mm equivalent f/1.8 lens, the same 8K-capable sensor as the Insta360 X6 but with notably better image quality from the lens.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.so_what: Optics rather than sensor drive the quality gap in this category.

insights.claim: The Luna Ultra can shoot 4K/120 fps in log, which the DJI Osmo cannot, though the Osmo reaches 4K/240 fps; the Osmo Pocket 4P offers 17 stops of dynamic range and D-Log 2.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.so_what: Spec trade-offs split the two lineups by use case.

insights.claim: The Luna's detachable OLED front panel with controls works remotely up to roughly 66 feet, a differentiator from the Osmo Pocket 4 for self-filming.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.quote: a detachable front panel with the OLED screen

insights.claim: Digital zoom on the Ultra visibly degrades quality, but an external zoom attachment adds 1.5X optical for 4.5X total with almost no discernible loss.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson

insights.claim: The target users are solo filmmakers, journalists and content creators, and buyers who move a lot may prefer the waterproof Insta360 X6 for its 360-degree reframing flexibility.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson

insights.claim: Drawbacks are a small screen that makes advanced settings fiddly and a non-replaceable battery; the tester recorded 2 hours 55 minutes of 4K/24 fps footage.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
